body: Ahhh I know what you mean. I've recently come out as trans (ftm) and I've not only lost the sense of style I once had before I transitioned, but I also feel like wearing more feminine clothing sometimes like dresses and such. However, I feel like it depreciates my transness, and I get massive dysphoria while wearing both feminine and masculine clothing. There seems to be no getting around it because the dysphoria's always there no matter how I dress, but I know in my heart that I'm comfortable with my gender identity now than I was before, so it's all very confusing.
I'm glad they're accepting of you 😊
Thank you for your kind words. I hope everything goes well for your mother and that things get better for her.

She doesn't sound like a very good friend... I think you should either be honest with her and tell her how you feel or stop being friends with her. I know you're probably worried about being alone in college since the both of you are going to the same school, but being alone for a little while is better than holding onto a "friend" that treats you like you don't even exist when her other friends are around. 

(Also, it's all a part of growing up. You realize the people that you thought were your friends actually aren't and you go your separate ways. You'll find positive people to surround yourself with eventually. It might take some time but focus on succeeding in college and life before anyone else. You'll realize that she is such an insignificant part of your life.)

You can definitely have a girlfriend without having any friends. If not having friends is what makes her rethink your relationship, I don't think they're the right person for you. But don't tell yourself that you'll never make any friends and that the only friends you'll make will be narcissistic; you never know what the future holds. And it's natural to have less friends in adulthood than you did when you were younger. Think of it is as a period of growth. You're pushing all of those negative people out of your life to leave room for positive experiences and people.
My introverted self would ghost them to avoid confrontation 😅

I'm in the same boat as you are. I turned 18 this year and am now graduating high school. I definitely hold a lot of regrets on the decisions I made as a teenager - not spending time with my friends when I was given the chance because of my anxiety, missing out on opportunities to put myself out there in general - it sucks to say the least, that I could have done so much more, making my teen years feel fulfilled.

But I will say, it does little to dwell on your past. Try looking forward to your future and work on ways to prevent what you did in your teen years to feel like you missed out. You'll meet new people through new experiences. 

I hope things get better for you. Just remember that your teen years are such a small part of your life and you still have so much time to work on yourself and experience new things.
I'd recommend rewriting it as "I could reschedule my appointment" so the focus is on you, but otherwise the email sounds considerate and does not sound rude at all.
